title: One Day in Victoria
name: Highlights of Victoria
meta: See Victoria in one day with an easy walk from the Inner Harbour to Beacon Hill Park, plus time for Chinatown and a seafood dinner.
intro: Victoria is a great place to explore on foot, especially around the Inner Harbour and downtown. If you only have one day, you can still see some of the city’s best-known sights without rushing from one end of the region to the other. This is a good plan for a first visit or a short stop if you like old streets, waterfront views, and somewhere to sit for coffee. If you’re arriving at Swartz Bay that morning, leave time to get downtown before you start sightseeing.

days.heading: Morning
paras: Start at the Inner Harbour and walk past the Parliament Buildings. Cross over to Government Street for coffee, then keep walking north to Chinatown. Fan Tan Alley is a quick detour. If the alley is busy, spend a little more time around the shops on Fisgard Street.

days.heading: Afternoon
paras: Grab lunch downtown, then head south through Beacon Hill Park. Follow the park paths toward Dallas Road if you want an open-water view. On a wet day, trade the park for the Royal BC Museum near the harbor.

days.heading: Evening
paras: Walk through James Bay to Fisherman’s Wharf for a bite if vendors are open. For a sit-down dinner with more choices, head back toward the Inner Harbour.

stops.name: Inner Harbour
stops.text: Start on the causeway for a view of the Parliament Buildings.

stops.name: Fan Tan Alley
stops.text: Turn off Fisgard Street for this short Chinatown detour.

stops.name: Dallas Road
stops.text: Add this waterfront stretch after Beacon Hill Park if you still feel like walking.

tips: Start near the Inner Harbour and leave the car parked for the day.
Check Fisherman’s Wharf vendor hours before counting on it for dinner.

faqs.q: Can you see Victoria in one day?
a: Yes. The harbor, Chinatown, and Beacon Hill Park make a full first day. Save Butchart Gardens for another visit or swap it in for the afternoon.

faqs.q: Do you need a car in downtown Victoria?
a: No. This route is walkable. If you arrive by ferry at Swartz Bay, plan your transfer into the city before the day starts.

faqs.q: What can you do for free in Victoria?
a: Walk the Inner Harbour, explore Chinatown, and follow park paths through Beacon Hill Park.

faqs.q: What can you do in Victoria when it rains?
a: Visit the Royal BC Museum, then stop for lunch or coffee near the harbor.

faqs.q: Where should you stay for a one-day visit?
a: Stay downtown near the Inner Harbour or Government Street to reach most stops on foot.

title: One Day in Vancouver
name: Vancouver by the Water
meta: Spend one day in Vancouver on the Stanley Park Seawall, at Granville Island Public Market, and around Gastown or English Bay.
intro: Vancouver is the kind of city where you can spend most of the day by the water and still feel like you’ve seen a lot. With one day, the waterfront around downtown and False Creek gives you an easy introduction to the city. It’s a good fit for first-time visitors who like to walk, browse a market, and leave time for a meal. The distances can sneak up on you, so use transit for the longer stretches if you want to save your feet.

days.heading: Morning
paras: Get coffee in the West End and enter Stanley Park near Coal Harbour. Walk a short stretch to the totem poles at Brockton Point, or rent a bike for a longer ride. Check posted directions and closures before setting out.

days.heading: Afternoon
paras: Head to Granville Island for the Public Market. Pick up lunch and sit outside by False Creek if the weather holds. A small passenger ferry is a fun way to cross the creek if the route fits. Check the last sailing if you plan to come back that way.

days.heading: Evening
paras: Walk through Gastown for dinner and a look at the old brick streets. If the sky is clear and you’d rather stay outside, head to English Bay for sunset and eat in the West End.

stops.name: Brockton Point
stops.text: Make the totem poles your turn-around point on a short Seawall walk.

stops.name: Granville Island Public Market
stops.text: Pick up a few things for lunch and eat by False Creek if it’s dry.

stops.name: English Bay
stops.text: End here if sunset by the water sounds better than a second downtown walk.

tips: Pick up a rental bike near the park if you plan to ride. Follow posted cycle directions and detours.
Give the market more time around lunch and check the last False Creek ferry before relying on it.

faqs.q: Is one day enough for Vancouver?
a: It’s enough for Stanley Park, Granville Island, and one evening stop. Give the North Shore its own day.

faqs.q: Can you get around without a car?
a: Yes. Walk, take transit, or use a False Creek ferry. Check the small ferries’ fares separately.

faqs.q: Can you walk the whole Stanley Park Seawall in one day?
a: Yes. If you also want time for Granville Island and dinner downtown, walk a shorter stretch or rent a bike.

faqs.q: What can you do in Vancouver on a rainy day?
a: Start with the covered Public Market and spend the afternoon at the Vancouver Art Gallery if open.

faqs.q: Where should you stay for a short Vancouver visit?
a: The West End is handy for Stanley Park. Downtown near a transit stop makes it easier to reach your other stops.

title: One Day in Tofino
name: Tofino’s Beaches and Rainforest
meta: Make the most of one day in Tofino with coffee by the harbor, a walk at Chesterman Beach, and a stop at Long Beach or the Rainforest Trail.
intro: Tofino is a small town, but the beaches are a big part of the visit. If you have one day, give yourself time for a proper walk on the sand and a chance to see the rainforest nearby. This suits anyone who’s already on the coast and wants an easy day outdoors. Bring a warm layer even if it feels mild in town, and check the tide and surf before choosing a beach.

days.heading: Morning
paras: Start with coffee downtown, then walk down to the waterfront to see the boats in Clayoquot Sound. Drive out to Chesterman Beach for a walk along the sand. Dress for wind even if it feels mild in town.

days.heading: Afternoon
paras: Have lunch near the beaches or in town. Head south to Pacific Rim National Park Reserve for Long Beach and, if trail conditions allow, one loop of the Rainforest Trail. The forest is a good choice on a wet day, as long as there are no wind closures.

days.heading: Evening
paras: Return to Tofino for dinner. On a clear day, you can fit in a last walk at Chesterman Beach before dark. During rough surf, watch from a safe viewpoint and stay back from the water and driftwood.

stops.name: Tofino waterfront
stops.text: Get coffee near town and look out over Clayoquot Sound.

stops.name: Chesterman Beach
stops.text: Make this your long beach walk if surf and tides are suitable.

stops.name: Rainforest Trail
stops.text: Choose one open boardwalk loop for a short forest walk.

tips: Check Parks Canada’s trail notices, tides, and swell forecast before you leave. Stay off the beach when the tide or swell is high.
Keep a rain shell and dry shoes in the car. A wet beach walk feels better when you can change before dinner.

faqs.q: Can you visit Tofino in a day?
a: Yes, if you’re already on the west coast or nearby. A Vancouver round trip is best spread over several days.

faqs.q: Do you need a pass for Long Beach?
a: Plan to get a Parks Canada entry pass for your visit to the Long Beach Unit. Check current admission and trail conditions before you go.

faqs.q: Which beaches should you see on your first visit?
a: Chesterman is close to Tofino. Long Beach gives you a second stretch of coast in the national park reserve.

faqs.q: Can you fit a surf lesson into one day?
a: Yes. Make it your morning outing and choose either Long Beach or the rainforest for the afternoon.

faqs.q: What should you do in Tofino during a storm?
a: Watch from an open, designated viewing area or from indoors and follow local closure notices.

title: One Day in Ucluelet
name: Ucluelet’s Lighthouse and Harbor
meta: Spend one day in Ucluelet on the Wild Pacific Trail, by the harbor, and at Big Beach, with an easy indoor stop if it rains.
intro: Ucluelet is a good place to slow down. You can watch the waves from the bluffs, then be back at the harbor for lunch without having to cross town all day. One day is plenty for a first visit if you like short walks and time to stop at the viewpoints. Families can keep the walks short, too. If it’s been windy, check trail notices before heading out and give the water plenty of space.

days.heading: Morning
paras: Start on the Lighthouse Loop of the Wild Pacific Trail. Pause at the marked viewpoints near Amphitrite Point. The loop has plenty of places to stop, so leave time to watch the waves from the trail.

days.heading: Afternoon
paras: Have lunch by the harbor and check whether the Ucluelet Aquarium is open. If you want more time outside, try the Brown’s Beach to Ancient Cedars section of the Wild Pacific Trail. Drive between trail sections if you want to save walking time.

days.heading: Evening
paras: Take a short walk at Big Beach if conditions are calm, then head into town for dinner. When the sea is rough, keep to viewpoints and stay off wet rocks and logs.

stops.name: Amphitrite Point
stops.text: Stop at the marked Lighthouse Loop viewpoints.

stops.name: Ucluelet Aquarium
stops.text: Make it your harbor stop if open, especially if you’re traveling with children.

stops.name: Brown’s Beach
stops.text: Start here for a second Wild Pacific Trail walk and turn back when you’re ready.

tips: Use signed viewpoints and stay clear of rocks and logs when waves are rough.
The Wild Pacific Trail has separate sections. Drive between them if your group wants to save its energy for the views.

faqs.q: Is Ucluelet worth visiting for one day?
a: Yes. The Lighthouse Loop and harbor give you a feel for town without a long drive between stops.

faqs.q: Can you see Tofino and Ucluelet in one day?
a: Yes, with one main stop in each town. Start in Ucluelet, stop at Long Beach, and finish in Tofino if you’re staying there.

faqs.q: Which part of the Wild Pacific Trail is best for a first visit?
a: Start with the Lighthouse Loop. It’s easy to follow and has several places to pause.

faqs.q: Is the Wild Pacific Trail free?
a: Yes. You can walk the public trail without paying for admission.

faqs.q: What can you do in Ucluelet if it rains?
a: Visit the aquarium when it’s open or have a long lunch by the harbor. Save the viewpoints for when conditions improve.

title: One Day in Whistler
name: Whistler Village to the Peaks
meta: Explore Whistler in one day with a Village stroll, a gondola ride when lifts run, and time by Lost Lake or at a local museum.
intro: Whistler is a mountain town with plenty to do down in the Village, too. With one day, choose one thing you really want to do, like riding the gondola, and leave time to look around. This works well for first-time visitors, especially if you’re coming from Vancouver and have to drive back that evening. Check the lift hours before making plans. If you’re here to ski, it’s easy to spend the whole day on the mountain.

days.heading: Morning
paras: Get coffee near Village Stroll and check the mountain forecast before buying a sightseeing ticket. If lifts are running and the peaks are clear, ride up early. In winter, a ski day can fill the whole schedule on its own.

days.heading: Afternoon
paras: Walk to Lost Lake when the route is suitable for walking. In winter, check which trails are open to walkers and which are set aside for skiing. For an indoor afternoon, visit the Squamish Lil’wat Cultural Centre or the Audain Art Museum if open.

days.heading: Evening
paras: Eat in Whistler Village. If you’re driving back to Vancouver, give yourself time for the Sea-to-Sky Highway and check road conditions before leaving.

stops.name: Village Stroll
stops.text: Start here for coffee and finish nearby for dinner.

stops.name: Whistler Blackcomb
stops.text: Choose a sightseeing ride or a ski day when lifts run.

stops.name: Squamish Lil’wat Cultural Centre
stops.text: Make this your main afternoon stop if clouds cover the peaks.

tips: Check lift hours and the last ride down before heading up.
Leave time for the drive back on Highway 99, especially if you’re adding a stop in Squamish.

faqs.q: Is Whistler worth a day trip from Vancouver?
a: Yes. Start early and pick either a few highway stops or a longer visit on the mountain.

faqs.q: Can you visit Whistler without skiing?
a: Yes. Village paths, museums, and sightseeing lifts can fill the day. Check the lift calendar, especially in spring and fall.

faqs.q: Is the PEAK 2 PEAK Gondola open year-round?
a: Its schedule changes with the season. Check the resort’s hours for your dates.

faqs.q: What can you do for free in Whistler Village?
a: Walk the pedestrian streets, explore around the Village, or follow an open Valley Trail section.

faqs.q: Can you visit Whistler as a day trip without a car?
a: Yes. Book a coach from Vancouver and check your last ride back before making dinner plans.

title: One Day in Kelowna
name: Kelowna From Trestles to the Lake
meta: Spend one day in Kelowna along Okanagan Lake, at Myra Canyon, or at a West Kelowna winery. Here’s how to pick a route that fits.
intro: Kelowna makes an easy day trip if you like a bit of country with your city. The waterfront is a good place to spend a few hours, and the old rail bridges above town are worth a look if you have a car. This day suits first-time visitors who like a walk or bike ride followed by lunch by the lake. On a hot day, get outside early. If the road to Myra Canyon is in poor shape, you can still have a good day downtown.

days.heading: Morning
paras: In dry, clear weather, drive up to the Myra Station trailhead for the Myra Canyon trestles. Walk or rent a bike in season. Even a short out-and-back gives you a look at the canyon. If the road or trail conditions are poor, start at Waterfront Park instead.

days.heading: Afternoon
paras: Have lunch downtown and walk along Okanagan Lake between Waterfront Park and City Park. If a winery is your main reason for visiting, trade part of the waterfront afternoon for a tasting in West Kelowna and arrange a sober ride.

days.heading: Evening
paras: Eat downtown and take one last walk by the lake. Stay near the water if you want to walk to dinner and skip a second drive.

stops.name: Myra Station
stops.text: Start here for a short out-and-back on the trestles.

stops.name: Waterfront Park
stops.text: Follow the shore toward downtown and make time to sit by the water.

stops.name: City Park
stops.text: Add a short lakefront walk after lunch if you’re staying in town.

tips: Go to the canyon early on hot days and check the access road before leaving.
Arrange a sober ride before you book tastings across the lake.

faqs.q: Can you do Kelowna in a day without a car?
a: Yes if you focus on downtown and the waterfront. Arrange a ride or tour for Myra Canyon or wineries.

faqs.q: Is Myra Canyon worth it if you don’t bike?
a: Yes. Start at Myra Station and walk as far as you like before turning back. Check current road and trail conditions.

faqs.q: What can families do in Kelowna in one day?
a: Keep to the downtown lakefront for a park, a picnic, and time by the water.

faqs.q: Can you rent a bike at Myra Canyon?
a: Rentals are offered in warmer months. Check opening dates or book in advance for a busy weekend.

faqs.q: Is West Kelowna worth adding to a short visit?
a: Yes if you’re here for wine. Give it most of the afternoon so you can enjoy the tasting and the ride back.

title: Tofino and Ucluelet Weekend Getaway
name: A Weekend on the Wild Coast
meta: Plan a Tofino and Ucluelet weekend with two nights, one base, beach walks, and a morning on Ucluelet’s Wild Pacific Trail.
intro: A weekend on Vancouver Island’s west coast is long enough for salty air, a couple of good walks, and dinner somewhere you can linger. Tofino is known for its wide beaches, while Ucluelet is where you’ll find rocky bluffs and a quieter harbor. Stay in one town for both nights, especially if you’re coming for a short break with your partner or friends. If you have an early ferry home, count back from check-in before making Sunday plans.

days.heading: Friday
paras: Make the drive your only big plan. Stop for groceries or dinner in Port Alberni if you’ll arrive late. Stock up on breakfast supplies so you can get outside early the next day.

days.heading: Saturday
paras: Give Tofino and the beaches a full day. Start at Chesterman Beach, have lunch in town, and stop at Long Beach or a Rainforest Trail loop in the afternoon. If you’re staying in Ucluelet, book dinner back in town so you can end the day near your room.

days.heading: Sunday
paras: Walk Ucluelet’s Lighthouse Loop and grab lunch by the harbor before heading home. If you have a ferry to catch from Nanaimo, build in time for Highway 4, fuel, and terminal check-in. Move the hike to Saturday if you have an early sailing.

stops.name: Chesterman Beach
stops.text: Give this the best beach weather on Saturday.

stops.name: Long Beach or the Rainforest Trail
stops.text: Pick one park stop on the drive between towns.

stops.name: Lighthouse Loop
stops.text: Save this for Sunday morning if you have a late ferry.

tips: Book Friday and Saturday at the same place so you can leave your bags unpacked.
Fuel in Port Alberni and check Highway 4 before each crossing.

faqs.q: Is it better to stay in Tofino or Ucluelet?
a: Pick the town where you want to spend your evenings. You can visit both from a single base.

faqs.q: Can you do this as a weekend trip from Vancouver?
a: Yes, but the ferry and drive take up much of Friday and Sunday. An extra night gives you more time on the coast.

faqs.q: Which town is quieter for a weekend stay?
a: Choose Ucluelet for a quiet harbor or bluff-side stay and easy access to the Lighthouse Loop.

faqs.q: What should you book first for a weekend getaway?
a: Lock in lodging and your ferry if you’re coming from the mainland. Then book any lessons or tours.

faqs.q: What can you do if the whole weekend is wet?
a: Use breaks in the weather for short walks and leave time for coffee, a long lunch, and the aquarium if open.

title: Two Days in Victoria
name: Victoria’s Harbor and Garden Paths
meta: Spend two days in Victoria exploring the Inner Harbour, Chinatown, Beacon Hill Park, and Butchart Gardens, with time for Sidney if you like.
intro: Victoria has plenty to keep you busy downtown, but two days also gives you time to see a little of the Saanich Peninsula. It’s a good length for a first visit, especially if you like both city walks and gardens. Keep the places you can reach on foot together and give the garden visit a morning of its own. If you’re leaving from Swartz Bay that day, check the ferry time before deciding how long to spend on the peninsula.

days.heading: Day 1: Inner Harbour, Chinatown, and James Bay
paras: Walk the Inner Harbour before it gets busy. Head up Government Street toward Chinatown for lunch, then make your way to Beacon Hill Park. If it rains, spend the afternoon at the Royal BC Museum. For dinner, try James Bay or the streets near the harbor.

days.heading: Day 2: Butchart Gardens and the peninsula
paras: Start at Butchart Gardens in Brentwood Bay. Give yourself time for the Sunken Garden and a break indoors if it’s cool. For lunch, stay near Brentwood Bay or head to Sidney for a walk along the waterfront. If you’re catching a ferry at Swartz Bay, check your terminal arrival time before adding Sidney.

stops.name: Chinatown
stops.text: Walk Fisgard Street and take a short detour through Fan Tan Alley.

stops.name: Butchart Gardens
stops.text: Allow time for the Sunken Garden and a sit-down break.

stops.name: Sidney waterfront
stops.text: Add a walk here if there’s time before your ferry or return to town.

tips: Book a downtown room so you can walk to dinner after both days.
Check garden admission and transit for your dates. Keep Sidney optional on the day you leave.

faqs.q: Is two days enough for Victoria?
a: Yes. Use one day for the city and one for the gardens. Add a third day if you also want a whale tour or a long day on the coast.

faqs.q: Can you visit Butchart Gardens without a car?
a: Yes. Look up the current transit connections or book a tour with transportation from Victoria.

faqs.q: How much time should you allow at Butchart Gardens?
a: Set aside a few hours so you can see the main paths and stop for a break.

faqs.q: Where should you stay for two days in Victoria?
a: The Inner Harbour and James Bay are both handy for the first day’s walks.

faqs.q: What’s a good rainy-day stop with children?
a: Try the Royal BC Museum or take a shorter harbor walk followed by lunch indoors.

title: Two Days in Vancouver
name: Vancouver’s Seawall and the North Shore
meta: See Vancouver in two days with Stanley Park, Granville Island, and a North Shore outing to Lynn Canyon or Capilano Suspension Bridge.
intro: Two days in Vancouver lets you see how close the city is to the forest. You can spend one day around the downtown waterfront and take the SeaBus across Burrard Inlet the next. It’s a good trip for first-time visitors who want to get around without a car. Pick one main North Shore stop so you have time to enjoy it, and check how you’ll get from the SeaBus to the trail or bridge you want to visit.

days.heading: Day 1: Stanley Park and False Creek
paras: Start on the Stanley Park Seawall from Coal Harbour. Walk to Brockton Point or rent a bike for more of the park. Head to Granville Island for lunch and a walk through the market. Finish with dinner on Main Street or in the West End, depending on where you’re staying.

days.heading: Day 2: North Vancouver
paras: Take the SeaBus from Waterfront Station to Lonsdale Quay. Continue by transit to Lynn Canyon for forest paths and the suspension bridge if open, or choose the paid Capilano Suspension Bridge Park. Give one stop most of the afternoon. Back at the quay, have dinner near the Shipyards and watch the city lights from across the inlet.

stops.name: Stanley Park Seawall
stops.text: Start from Coal Harbour and turn back whenever you like.

stops.name: Lynn Canyon or Capilano
stops.text: Pick one bridge and check access before crossing the inlet.

stops.name: The Shipyards
stops.text: End the second day near Lonsdale Quay for dinner and skyline views.

tips: Check your North Shore bus route before the SeaBus ride.
Leave dinner close to your last stop to cut travel time at the end of each day.

faqs.q: What can you do in Vancouver in two days without a car?
a: This route works by foot and transit. Check the onward bus for your North Shore stop before boarding the SeaBus.

faqs.q: What if it rains?
a: Keep the market and add the Museum of Vancouver or Vancouver Art Gallery. Check opening days before you go.

faqs.q: Which suspension bridge should you visit?
a: Pick Lynn Canyon for a forest walk when paths are open. Choose Capilano if you want a paid attraction with more planned stops.

faqs.q: Where can you see the Vancouver skyline?
a: Head to the waterfront near the Shipyards and look back across Burrard Inlet.

faqs.q: How much time should you spend at Granville Island?
a: Leave time for lunch and a walk around the shops. An hour or two works for most visitors.

title: Two Days in Whistler
name: Whistler Peaks and Lakes
meta: Plan two days in Whistler with Village time, mountain sightseeing or skiing, and a second day for Lost Lake or the Valley Trail.
intro: Whistler has a different feel up on the mountain than it does by the lakes. Two days gives you time for both, with evenings free for dinner in the Village. That’s a good fit for couples or families who want a big outing and a day that’s easier on the legs. Keep the days open enough to swap them if the weather changes. If you’re coming between seasons, check what’s open before you count on the lifts.

days.heading: Day 1: The Village and the mountain
paras: Get up early for skiing in winter or gondola sightseeing when summer lifts are running. Keep lunch on the mountain if you want more time up high. If lifts are closed, spend a few hours at the Squamish Lil’wat Cultural Centre and walk through Upper Village. Book dinner near your stay.

days.heading: Day 2: A slower day in the valley
paras: In warmer weather, rent a bike and ride a section of the Valley Trail to Rainbow Park on Alta Lake. If you’d rather walk, choose Lost Lake when pedestrian routes are open. In winter, check groomed trail rules or book a snowshoe outing. End at the Audain Art Museum if it’s open and you have time.

stops.name: Whistler Blackcomb
stops.text: Put skiing or lift sightseeing on the clearest day.

stops.name: Rainbow Park
stops.text: Follow an open Valley Trail section to Alta Lake in warmer months.

stops.name: Audain Art Museum
stops.text: Keep it in mind for a wet or smoky afternoon and check hours.

tips: Stay near the Village so you can leave the car parked.
In winter, check where pedestrians can walk around Lost Lake before leaving the Village.

faqs.q: Is two days enough in Whistler?
a: Yes for one mountain day and one valley day. Add a night if you also want time in Squamish.

faqs.q: Where should you stay without a car?
a: Whistler Village or Upper Village puts you close to dining and the main lift bases. Check shuttle schedules for trips farther out.

faqs.q: Can you swap the days around?
a: Yes. Take the clearest open lift day and use the other for a museum, shops, or a valley outing.

faqs.q: Is Whistler good for a summer weekend?
a: Yes. Lake parks, paved paths, and mountain sightseeing give you several ways to spend two days.

faqs.q: What can you do after skiing?
a: Have a meal in the Village, take a short walk, or visit a museum if it’s still open.

title: Two Days in the Okanagan
name: Okanagan Lakes and the Naramata Bench
meta: Plan a two-day Okanagan trip with Kelowna’s waterfront, Myra Canyon, and a day of lakeside stops around Penticton and Naramata.
intro: Two days is enough to get a feel for the Okanagan if you stick to one stretch of the lake. Kelowna has the busier waterfront, while Penticton and Naramata are good places to slow down. This trip works for couples or families who want some time outdoors and don’t mind a short drive between towns. Decide whether your afternoons are for the beach or a tasting. If it’s a tasting, sort out your ride early.

days.heading: Day 1: Kelowna and Myra Canyon
paras: Start at Myra Station if the road is suitable for your car. Walk a short stretch of the trestles or rent a bike in season. Go back downtown for lunch and spend the late afternoon between Waterfront Park and City Park. Stay downtown for a walk to dinner.

days.heading: Day 2: Penticton and Naramata
paras: Drive south along the west side of Okanagan Lake. Stop in Peachland for coffee by the water, then continue to Penticton for lunch. Spend the afternoon on the Naramata Bench with one or two tasting stops, or take a walk along the lake in Penticton. Book a ride if you plan to drink.

stops.name: Myra Canyon
stops.text: Choose a short trestle walk or a longer bike ride.

stops.name: Peachland waterfront
stops.text: Stop for coffee on the way south.

stops.name: Naramata Bench
stops.text: Pick a tasting or a walk on the Kettle Valley Rail Trail above the lake.

tips: Stay in Penticton on the second night if you want to walk to dinner after visiting the bench.
In hot weather, walk the trestles early and leave the afternoon for shade or the lake.

faqs.q: Should you stay in Kelowna or Penticton?
a: Choose Kelowna for city dining and Myra Canyon. Choose Penticton if you want more time near the beach and Naramata.

faqs.q: Can you visit the Okanagan without going to wineries?
a: Yes. Swap the tastings for Penticton’s waterfront, a beach afternoon, or a stroll in Naramata village.

faqs.q: Where should you stop between Kelowna and Penticton?
a: Peachland is an easy place for coffee, a meal, or a stretch by the lake.

faqs.q: Do you need a car for this two-day route?
a: A car helps with Myra Canyon and the turnoffs. Book separate transport for tastings if you plan to drink.

faqs.q: Is the Naramata Bench worth visiting without a tasting?
a: Yes. Walk an open section of the rail trail or head down to Naramata village for a picnic.

title: Three Days in Tofino and Ucluelet
name: Beaches, Big Trees, and the Wild Pacific Trail
meta: Spend three days in Tofino and Ucluelet with a beach day, rainforest walks in Pacific Rim, and a full day around Ucluelet’s rocky coast.
intro: Three days is a comfortable amount of time to visit both Tofino and Ucluelet. You can take a long beach walk, spend some time in the rainforest, and still get to know the quieter side of the coast. The towns are close enough to visit from one base, which works well for first-timers and anyone who likes to leave room for a surf lesson or boat trip. Keep at least one day loose so you can work around the weather.

days.heading: Day 1: Tofino and Chesterman Beach
paras: Start downtown for coffee and a walk by the docks. Spend the afternoon at Chesterman Beach or book a surf lesson with a local school. Have dinner in Tofino while you’re already at the north end of the route.

days.heading: Day 2: Pacific Rim National Park Reserve
paras: Start at Long Beach and take a picnic lunch. In the afternoon, visit an open Rainforest Trail loop. If you have time and the access trail is open, add a walk at Wickaninnish Beach. On a stormy day, choose safe viewpoints and keep well away from the surf.

days.heading: Day 3: Ucluelet and the Wild Pacific Trail
paras: Walk the Lighthouse Loop first. Have lunch by the harbor, then choose the aquarium if open or an out-and-back walk from Brown’s Beach. If this is also a ferry day, keep the afternoon stop optional.

stops.name: Chesterman Beach
stops.text: Start here for a walk or make a lesson your main Tofino outing.

stops.name: Long Beach and Rainforest Trail
stops.text: Pair one stretch of sand with one open forest loop.

stops.name: Wild Pacific Trail
stops.text: Choose the Lighthouse Loop and add Brown’s Beach if time allows.

tips: Put boat outings on the best forecast day and leave room to move the beach plans.
Check park admission, surf, and tides. Skip exposed beaches when winds and waves are high.

faqs.q: Where should you stay for three days?
a: Either town works. Stay in Tofino for a beach or surf trip, or in Ucluelet for the lighthouse and an easier start toward Highway 4 on the way out.

faqs.q: What should you book ahead?
a: Book lodging and any boat tours or surf lessons first. Check park passes and ferry space as you firm up your dates.

faqs.q: Should you split your stay between Tofino and Ucluelet?
a: One base works well for three days. Pick where you’d like to spend your evenings.

faqs.q: What should you do in Pacific Rim with just half a day?
a: Walk a short stretch of Long Beach and one open Rainforest Trail loop if conditions allow.

faqs.q: Can you do this trip in winter?
a: Yes if you build it around conditions and open sites. Consider a room with an ocean view and fewer fixed outdoor plans.

title: Three Days on Vancouver Island
name: An Easy Island Escape From Victoria to Nanaimo
meta: See southern and central Vancouver Island in three days with Victoria, Cowichan Bay, and a Nanaimo waterfront finish.
intro: Vancouver Island is bigger than it looks on a map. With three days, the east side is a good choice if you like harbor walks and small towns and want to spend more time out of the car. Victoria and Nanaimo make useful start and end points, with the Cowichan Valley in between. This works well for a long weekend or a first Island trip. If you’re bringing a car on the ferry, check both terminal locations when you book.

days.heading: Day 1: Victoria
paras: Start at the Inner Harbour, walk to Chinatown for lunch, then head south to Beacon Hill Park. If you’re coming in on a late ferry, keep the afternoon to downtown and save the park for another visit. Sleep in Victoria.

days.heading: Day 2: Cowichan Valley
paras: Drive over the Malahat and go to Cowichan Bay for a walk along the village’s waterfront. Pick up lunch there, then head to Duncan for the downtown totem poles or check the BC Forest Discovery Centre’s opening hours. Sleep in the Duncan area.

days.heading: Day 3: Ladysmith and Nanaimo
paras: Walk Transfer Beach in Ladysmith, then follow the highway north to Nanaimo. Park downtown, try a Nanaimo bar, and walk the Harbourfront Walkway. Leave enough time to reach the terminal on your reservation.

stops.name: Inner Harbour
stops.text: Keep the first day’s sights close together in Victoria.

stops.name: Cowichan Bay
stops.text: Walk the village waterfront and stay for lunch.

stops.name: Nanaimo Harbourfront Walkway
stops.text: Finish here before catching your ferry if time allows.

tips: Stay near Duncan on the second night so you can reach Ladysmith without an early start.
Double-check your Nanaimo terminal. Departure Bay and Duke Point are in different places.

faqs.q: Is three days enough for Vancouver Island?
a: It works for one part of the Island. Add more nights if Tofino or Ucluelet is a must.

faqs.q: Which ferries fit this route?
a: From the mainland, use Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay to start. From Nanaimo, pick Departure Bay for Horseshoe Bay or Duke Point for Tsawwassen.

faqs.q: What’s a good stop between Duncan and Nanaimo?
a: Transfer Beach in Ladysmith makes an easy leg stretch or picnic stop.

faqs.q: Can you add Butchart Gardens to three days?
a: Yes. Give it most of Day 1 and keep downtown Victoria to an evening harbor walk.

faqs.q: Do you need a car for this Island route?
a: A car makes it easier to stop in the smaller communities and reach your chosen ferry terminal.

title: Three Days in Victoria and the Cowichan Valley
name: Harbor, Gardens, and Cowichan Backroads
meta: Spend three days in Victoria and the Cowichan Valley with harbor walks, Butchart Gardens, and a day around Cowichan Bay and Duncan.
intro: Victoria and the Cowichan Valley make a good pair if your idea of a trip includes gardens, little shops, and a long lunch. Three days lets you enjoy the city and the peninsula before setting aside time for the towns over the Malahat. This route works well for a couple or a small group who prefer short walks and their own pace. Check opening days if you have a farm shop, tasting room, or garden you’re keen to visit.

days.heading: Day 1: Victoria on foot
paras: Walk from the Inner Harbour to Chinatown. After lunch, make your way to Beacon Hill Park and Dallas Road, or spend the afternoon at the Royal BC Museum if it’s wet. Have dinner downtown.

days.heading: Day 2: Gardens and Sidney
paras: Start at Butchart Gardens and leave time for the paths that branch off the main route. Head to Sidney for lunch and a walk by the water. If you prefer fewer stops, linger at the gardens and go back to Victoria for dinner.

days.heading: Day 3: Cowichan Bay and Duncan
paras: Drive to Cowichan Bay for coffee and a waterfront walk. In Duncan, view the downtown totem poles and read the signs as you go. For your last stop, pick a farm shop or book one winery tasting with a sober driver.

stops.name: Butchart Gardens
stops.text: Start early enough to take your time in the Sunken Garden.

stops.name: Cowichan Bay
stops.text: Plan lunch near the water and a walk through the village.

stops.name: Downtown Duncan
stops.text: Follow the totem poles and pause to read the signs.

tips: Check farm shop and tasting hours before picking your last stop.
Keep the drive over the Malahat flexible if you have rain, traffic, or an early dinner booking.

faqs.q: Can you visit the Cowichan Valley as a day trip from Victoria?
a: Yes. Cowichan Bay and Duncan make a good pair. Allow extra road time on the Malahat during peak traffic.

faqs.q: Do you need a car?
a: Victoria and the gardens can work without one. A car or a booked tour helps for the valley villages and farm stops.

faqs.q: Is it worth staying overnight in the Cowichan Valley?
a: Yes if you want dinner in the valley or a slower start the next morning.

faqs.q: Can you visit Cowichan Bay and Duncan in one day?
a: Yes. Give one stop the morning and the other the afternoon.

faqs.q: What should you do on a rainy day in Victoria?
a: Visit the Royal BC Museum and keep the harbor walk short if showers are heavy.

title: Three Days in Whistler
name: Three Days in the Whistler Peaks
meta: Use three days in Whistler for a mountain day, a lake or bike day, and time for art, culture, or a stop in Squamish.
intro: Three days in Whistler gives you time to enjoy the Village and wait for a good day up high. That little bit of slack matters when the peaks are in cloud or you’re still getting used to your ski boots. It’s a good trip for first-timers who want a full mountain day and time to look around down below. If you’re visiting in spring or fall, check the lift dates and keep a lake walk or museum in mind.

days.heading: Day 1: Get to know the Village
paras: Walk Village Stroll and visit the Squamish Lil’wat Cultural Centre if open. Leave the afternoon loose for a coffee, rental pickup, and a walk through Upper Village. That way you can start early on the mountain the next day.

days.heading: Day 2: Ski or take the gondola
paras: In winter, ski or book a lesson suited to your level. In summer, take the sightseeing lifts when they’re running and choose an open trail that fits your group. If cloud covers the peaks, spend more time in the valley and check the forecast for tomorrow.

days.heading: Day 3: Lakes or Squamish
paras: In warmer weather, ride the Valley Trail to Rainbow Park or take a short walk near Lost Lake. In winter, check walking routes or visit the Audain Art Museum. If you’re driving south, leave early enough to stop at Shannon Falls near Squamish.

stops.name: Squamish Lil’wat Cultural Centre

stops.name: Whistler Blackcomb
stops.text: Choose skiing or sightseeing for your full day.

stops.name: Shannon Falls
stops.text: Add a short walk on the way south if time allows.

tips: Pick up rental gear the night before if the shop allows it.
Check the last lift down and leave the third afternoon open for travel.

faqs.q: What month is best to visit Whistler?
a: Pick winter for skiing and summer for the lakes and bike trails. Check lift hours in the spring and fall between seasons.

faqs.q: Can you fill three days in Whistler without skiing?
a: Yes. Mix one gondola or museum day with the Village, lake paths, and a stop in Squamish.

faqs.q: Can you visit Whistler in the off-season?
a: Yes. Make the Village, museums, and open valley paths your main plans and treat gondola rides as optional.

faqs.q: Where can you spend time by a lake?
a: Try an open Valley Trail route near Lost Lake or take a ride to Rainbow Park.

faqs.q: Which day should you stop in Squamish?
a: Use the drive back south if you have a late departure. Otherwise, stop on the way up and keep Day 3 short.

title: Three Days in the Okanagan
name: From Kelowna to the Desert Lakes
meta: Follow a three-day Okanagan route from Kelowna to Penticton and Osoyoos, with trestles, lakeside walks, and optional wine stops.
intro: The Okanagan changes as you go south. Around Kelowna, there’s lots to do by the lake. Near Osoyoos, the hills look drier and the towns feel smaller. Three days gives first-time visitors enough time to notice the change, with room for short walks and a tasting if that’s your thing. Traveling in one direction keeps the driving down. If you’re flying out of Kelowna, leave time to come back north.

days.heading: Day 1: Kelowna and Myra Canyon
paras: Walk or bike a section of Myra Canyon from Myra Station if the access road and trail are in good shape. Return to downtown Kelowna for a late lunch and a stroll along Okanagan Lake.

days.heading: Day 2: Penticton and the Naramata Bench
paras: Stop at the Peachland waterfront on the way south. In Penticton, walk by Okanagan Beach and pick up lunch. Visit a winery on the Naramata Bench with a sober driver or walk a section of the Kettle Valley Rail Trail.

days.heading: Day 3: Oliver and Osoyoos
paras: Head south to Oliver, then continue to Osoyoos for a waterfront walk. If open, visit the Nk’Mip Desert Cultural Centre to learn about the Osoyoos Indian Band and the plants and wildlife of the area. If you’re returning north the same day, skip the extra tasting stop.

stops.name: Naramata Bench
stops.text: Choose a tasting or a rail trail walk.

stops.name: Nk’Mip Desert Cultural Centre
stops.text: Make this your main Osoyoos stop if open.

tips: Pack water and plan exposed walks early in warm weather.
If you’re flying from Kelowna, check how much of Day 3 you can spend south of Penticton.

faqs.q: Is three days enough for the Okanagan?
a: Yes for a short trip through the main towns. Five days gives you more time at the lakes and fewer hotel changes.

faqs.q: When is a good time for this route?
a: Summer suits beach days. Spring and fall suit walks and tastings, with fewer daylight hours or shorter business hours to plan around.

faqs.q: Where should you stay on the second night?
a: Pick Penticton for easy access to Naramata or Osoyoos for more time at the south end.

faqs.q: Can you do this route with children?
a: Yes. Choose a short trestle walk, an afternoon at Okanagan Beach, and a stop at the cultural center if open.

faqs.q: What can you do on a hot Okanagan afternoon?
a: Take a long lunch indoors or choose a shaded stop by the lake. Save sunny trails for morning.

title: Five Days on Vancouver Island
name: Victoria to the Pacific Rim
meta: Plan five days on Vancouver Island from Victoria to the Pacific Rim, with stops in the Cowichan Valley and Cathedral Grove.
intro: Five days is enough to get a taste of Victoria and the west coast of Vancouver Island. Breaking up the drive on the east side gives you time in the smaller towns and keeps the trip out to the surf from feeling like one long day in the car. It’s a good route for a first visit if you like city walks as much as wild beaches. Give Highway 4 some extra time, especially on the day you’re catching a ferry.

days.heading: Day 1: Downtown Victoria
paras: Walk the Inner Harbour, Government Street, and Chinatown. Spend the afternoon at Beacon Hill Park or the Royal BC Museum. Sleep downtown so you can walk to dinner.

days.heading: Day 2: Cowichan Bay and Parksville
paras: Cross the Malahat and have lunch in Cowichan Bay. Choose downtown Duncan or a short stop in Ladysmith on the way north. Spend the night near Parksville.

days.heading: Day 3: Cathedral Grove to Ucluelet
paras: Check MacMillan Park advisories before a Cathedral Grove stop. If the parking area is full, keep going and take a break in Port Alberni. Reach Ucluelet in time for the Lighthouse Loop before dark. Sleep on the west coast.

days.heading: Day 4: Pacific Rim and Tofino
paras: Walk at Long Beach early, then choose a Rainforest Trail loop or a stop at Chesterman Beach. Have lunch in Tofino and stay on the west coast again.

days.heading: Day 5: Return to Nanaimo
paras: Leave the coast after breakfast. Stop in Port Alberni for fuel, then go straight to your Nanaimo terminal if you have a reservation. Take a waterfront walk only if you have a comfortable buffer.

stops.name: Cowichan Bay
stops.text: Stop here for lunch before driving north.

stops.name: Cathedral Grove
stops.text: Walk among the tall trees if parking and trails are open.

stops.name: Lighthouse Loop and Long Beach
stops.text: Use separate days for these two main coastal stops.

tips: Keep your ferry day free of long walks or tours.
Buy food and fuel in Port Alberni before the last leg west.

faqs.q: Where should you stay for five days?
a: Try one night in Victoria, one around Parksville, and two on the west coast.

faqs.q: Is five days enough to see Vancouver Island?
a: Yes for the south and Pacific Rim. Give the north Island a longer trip of its own.

faqs.q: What’s the best place for a stop between Parksville and Ucluelet?
a: Try Cathedral Grove if there’s parking. Port Alberni is a good place for food and fuel.

faqs.q: Can you do this in reverse?
a: Yes. Start in Nanaimo, spend two nights on the west coast, and finish in Victoria.

faqs.q: Should you visit both Tofino and Ucluelet?
a: Yes. Use Ucluelet for the Lighthouse Loop and Tofino for a meal and a beach walk.

title: Vancouver, Tofino, and Ucluelet in Five Days
name: City Seawall to Pacific Surf
meta: Start with a day in Vancouver, then take the ferry to Nanaimo for three nights near Tofino and Ucluelet before heading back.
intro: Five days gives you a little city time in Vancouver and a real break by the surf in Tofino and Ucluelet. This works well for a first visit if you’re happy to spend part of the trip on the ferry and in the car. Stay in one place on the coast so you get two full days for the beaches and trails. Treat the ferry days as travel days, and leave a good gap before any flight home.

days.heading: Day 1: Vancouver waterfront
paras: Walk part of the Stanley Park Seawall and eat lunch at Granville Island. Pick up anything you need for the road trip before dinner.

days.heading: Day 2: Ferry to Nanaimo and Highway 4
paras: Take Horseshoe Bay to Departure Bay or Tsawwassen to Duke Point. Drive through Port Alberni and make this a travel day. If you arrive early, stop by the harbor near your hotel.

days.heading: Day 3: Tofino and the beaches
paras: Spend the morning at Chesterman Beach or book a surf lesson. Have lunch in town and walk a section of Long Beach on the way back.

days.heading: Day 4: Ucluelet and the rainforest
paras: Give the Lighthouse Loop the morning. Have lunch by the harbor and visit an open Rainforest Trail loop after lunch. On a rough-weather day, cut the beach stops and favor safe viewpoints.

days.heading: Day 5: West coast to Vancouver
paras: Drive to Nanaimo for your booked ferry. Leave a buffer for the winding road and terminal check-in. If you’re flying, leave the flight for the next day where possible.

stops.name: Stanley Park
stops.text: Walk a section of the Seawall on your city day.

stops.name: Chesterman Beach
stops.text: Make this your main beach walk or surf stop.

stops.name: Wild Pacific Trail
stops.text: Save the Lighthouse Loop for your Ucluelet morning.

tips: Stay in one place for all three west coast nights.
Book both ferry directions before adding timed outings around the crossings.

faqs.q: Can you do this trip without a car?
a: You can piece it together with booked transfers and local rides. This particular plan assumes a car from the mainland or Nanaimo.

faqs.q: What if you have an early flight home?
a: Sleep on the mainland the night before. A ferry crossing and a long drive leave little room for delays.

faqs.q: Which stop should you cut if a ferry is late?
a: Skip Cathedral Grove or any other stop you hoped to add on the transfer. Go straight to your west coast lodging.

faqs.q: Where can you stop for supplies before the coast?
a: Pick up groceries and fuel in Port Alberni on the way west.

faqs.q: Can you fit in a boat outing?
a: Yes. Use one full-day morning and save a beach or forest walk as the backup.

title: Victoria, Cowichan Valley, and Nanaimo
name: Gardens and Harbor Towns of Vancouver Island
meta: Follow the east side of Vancouver Island from Victoria to Nanaimo in four days, with gardens, a Cowichan Bay lunch, and a harbor walk.
intro: You can drive from Victoria to Nanaimo in part of a day, but it’s the smaller places along the way that make this trip worth stretching out. The Cowichan Valley is a good place to linger over lunch, and the gardens and waterfront walks give you easy ways to spend the rest of the time. Four days suits travelers who like a gentle pace and short drives. Check opening days for your favorite stops before you settle on dates.

days.heading: Day 1: Victoria’s old town
paras: Walk from the Inner Harbour to Chinatown. Try the Royal BC Museum in the afternoon or walk through James Bay to Beacon Hill Park. Stay downtown.

days.heading: Day 2: Butchart Gardens to the Cowichan Valley
paras: Visit the gardens in the morning. Cross the Malahat after lunch and settle in near Duncan or Cowichan Bay. Keep the evening free for a local dinner.

days.heading: Day 3: Cowichan Bay and Duncan
paras: Walk the bay’s main street, then have lunch by the water. Head to Duncan to see the downtown totem poles, or pick the BC Forest Discovery Centre if it’s open and your group wants a longer stop. Sleep in the valley again.

days.heading: Day 4: Ladysmith and Nanaimo
paras: Pause at Transfer Beach, then follow the highway to Nanaimo. Have lunch downtown and take a walk on the Harbourfront Walkway before your ferry or check-in.

stops.name: Butchart Gardens
stops.text: Make this your main stop before driving over the Malahat.

stops.name: Cowichan Bay and Duncan
stops.text: Pair a waterfront lunch with the downtown totem poles.

stops.name: Transfer Beach
stops.text: Break up the last drive with a short walk in Ladysmith.

tips: Book a valley stay for both nights to keep Day 3 easy.
Check Forest Discovery Centre hours before you plan the Duncan afternoon around it.

faqs.q: Can you drive this route in one day?
a: Yes, but four days leaves time to walk and eat in each place. With two days, skip the gardens or one valley stop.

faqs.q: Where is the best place to stay in the Cowichan Valley?
a: Cowichan Bay works for a quiet waterfront stay. Duncan is handy for the highway and services.

faqs.q: What can you do in Nanaimo before a ferry?
a: Try a Nanaimo bar downtown and walk a short part of the Harbourfront Walkway if time allows.

faqs.q: Where can you stop with children?
a: Try Beacon Hill Park, the BC Forest Discovery Centre when open, or Transfer Beach.

faqs.q: Which way should you drive the route?
a: Start near the ferry or airport that suits your plans. Reverse the daily order if you arrive in Nanaimo.

title: Five Days in the Okanagan
name: Five Days of Lakes and Vineyard Views
meta: Spend five days in the Okanagan with two bases, bike rides at Myra Canyon, beach time in Penticton, and a day trip to Osoyoos.
intro: The Okanagan is a good place to leave a few afternoons open. You might feel like a swim, a long lunch, or a walk between the vines once you see what the day is like. Five days works well for couples or families who want time by the lake and a choice of things to do. Two bases keep the driving down. In hot weather, do the exposed walks early and save the middle of the day for shade.

days.heading: Day 1: Kelowna waterfront
paras: Check in downtown and walk from Waterfront Park to City Park. Pick a patio for dinner if it’s warm enough.

days.heading: Day 2: Myra Canyon and West Kelowna
paras: Walk or bike the trestles from Myra Station if conditions are good. After lunch, choose one West Kelowna winery with a sober driver, or spend the rest of the day by the lake.

days.heading: Day 3: Peachland to Penticton
paras: Stop in Peachland for coffee and a waterfront walk. In Penticton, spend the afternoon at Okanagan Beach and have dinner downtown. Stay two nights.

days.heading: Day 4: Naramata Bench
paras: Walk part of the Kettle Valley Rail Trail in the morning. Book a winery lunch or tasting with a sober ride, or take a picnic down to Naramata village.

days.heading: Day 5: Oliver and Osoyoos
paras: Head south for a walk by Osoyoos Lake and visit the Nk’Mip Desert Cultural Centre if open. If you have a flight out of Kelowna, leave the south end for another trip or add a night.

stops.name: Myra Canyon
stops.text: Walk the trestles early or book bikes in season.

stops.name: Okanagan Beach
stops.text: Give the Penticton waterfront a full afternoon.

stops.name: Naramata Bench
stops.text: Pick a winery lunch, a rail trail walk, or a picnic in the village.

tips: Book sober transport for tasting days before setting your times.
Try a shorter morning walk if it’s hot and leave the middle of the day for shade.

faqs.q: What’s the best base for five days?
a: Kelowna and Penticton split the driving well. Pick Penticton alone if you care most about the south end.

faqs.q: What can families do instead of wine tasting?
a: Plan for beaches, the trestles, fruit stands in season, and shorter stretches of rail trail.

faqs.q: Can you visit Osoyoos as a day trip from Penticton?
a: Yes. Leave early enough to stop in Oliver or visit the cultural center if open.

faqs.q: Is Okanagan Lake or Skaha Lake better for a beach day?
a: Choose Okanagan Beach to stay near downtown Penticton. Pick Skaha Lake Park for a day at the south end of town.

faqs.q: Can you do this trip with one hotel?
a: Yes, especially from Penticton. Count on more driving for the Kelowna and Myra Canyon stops.

title: Vancouver and Whistler in Five Days
name: Vancouver and Whistler City-to-Summit Escape
meta: Spend five days in Vancouver and Whistler with two city days, a scenic drive through Squamish, and a full day on the mountain.
intro: Vancouver and Whistler are close enough to put on one trip, even if you only have five days. They work well together if you like a busy waterfront one day and a view of the mountains the next. This is a good first trip for anyone who wants city time and a full day in Whistler. Give the Sea-to-Sky drive some breathing room if you’re renting a car. A coach is an easy choice if you’re happy to go straight to the Village.

days.heading: Day 1: Stanley Park and English Bay
paras: Follow the Seawall from Coal Harbour or walk a short loop near the totem poles. Eat dinner in the West End and walk down to English Bay if the sky is clear.

days.heading: Day 2: Granville Island and False Creek
paras: Buy lunch at the Public Market and take a small ferry across the creek if sailing times fit. Spend the afternoon at a museum or walk the Olympic Village waterfront.

days.heading: Day 3: Sea-to-Sky Highway
paras: Leave Vancouver after breakfast. Stop at Shannon Falls and choose a second stop in Squamish for lunch or the Sea to Sky Gondola. Continue to Whistler for dinner.

days.heading: Day 4: Whistler mountain day
paras: Ski in winter or book sightseeing in summer if lifts are running. If the weather keeps you off the mountain, visit the Squamish Lil’wat Cultural Centre and explore Upper Village.

days.heading: Day 5: Valley Trail and the drive back
paras: Walk a section of the Valley Trail or go to the Audain Art Museum if open. Leave Whistler early if you’re headed to the airport. A final night in Vancouver works well before a morning flight.

stops.name: Stanley Park and Granville Island
stops.text: Spread these across the two city days.

stops.name: Shannon Falls
stops.text: Stop near Squamish for a short walk if the park is open.

stops.name: Whistler Blackcomb
stops.text: Use your full Whistler day for lifts or skiing when open.

tips: Pick up your rental car as you leave Vancouver if you’re using transit in the city.
Choose one longer Squamish outing so you still reach Whistler in time for dinner.

faqs.q: How many days should you spend in each place?
a: Two full days in Vancouver, one mountain day, and two travel days give each place time.

faqs.q: Is the Sea-to-Sky Highway worth driving?
a: Yes if you want to stop in Squamish. Check conditions and use designated pullouts for photos.

faqs.q: Is a car worth renting for this route?
a: Yes if you want to stop in Squamish. A coach works well if you mainly want to visit both towns.

faqs.q: What can you do if Whistler’s lifts are closed?
a: Walk the Village and an open Valley Trail section or visit the cultural center.

faqs.q: Where can you stop for lunch on the drive?
a: Squamish is a natural mid-route stop before the last leg to Whistler.

title: Seven Days on Vancouver Island
name: Island Harbors, Surf, and Waterfalls
meta: Use seven days on Vancouver Island to see Victoria, the Pacific Rim coast, and Campbell River, with time for a full day in each area.
intro: A week is enough to see how different Vancouver Island feels from one side to the other. There’s city life around Victoria, open surf on the west coast, and quieter water near Campbell River. This is a good first road trip for travelers who want a bit of each and are fine with a couple of longer drives. Staying more than one night in the coastal areas makes the drive worthwhile. Check Highway 4 and leave time to reach your final ferry.

days.heading: Day 1: Victoria
paras: Walk the Inner Harbour and Chinatown, then head to Beacon Hill Park. Stay downtown.

days.heading: Day 2: Gardens and Cowichan Bay
paras: Visit Butchart Gardens, then cross the Malahat for a late lunch or dinner in Cowichan Bay. Sleep near Duncan or Parksville, depending on how much driving you want.

days.heading: Day 3: Highway 4 to Ucluelet
paras: Stop in Port Alberni for fuel and food. Walk the Lighthouse Loop if you reach Ucluelet in daylight. Stay on the west coast.

days.heading: Day 4: Pacific Rim and Tofino
paras: Walk Long Beach and one open Rainforest Trail loop. Have dinner in Tofino or back near your room.

days.heading: Day 5: Cross to Campbell River
paras: Drive back through Port Alberni, then turn north on the east side. Stop for lunch near Parksville or Qualicum Beach. Stay in Campbell River.

days.heading: Day 6: Elk Falls and the waterfront
paras: Visit Elk Falls Provincial Park if trails are open. Leave the afternoon for the waterfront or book a guided wildlife outing that fits the season.

days.heading: Day 7: Nanaimo and the ferry
paras: Drive south, pick up lunch near Nanaimo’s harbor if time allows, and check in at the terminal on your booking.

stops.name: Butchart Gardens
stops.text: Start here before you cross the Malahat.

stops.name: Pacific Rim
stops.text: Pair a Long Beach walk with one open Rainforest Trail loop.

stops.name: Elk Falls
stops.text: Keep a morning free for the park when trails are open.

tips: Plan meals and fuel around Port Alberni both ways across Highway 4.
Stay in Campbell River on both nights so the wildlife or waterfall day needs little driving.

faqs.q: Is seven days enough for Vancouver Island?
a: Yes for Victoria, Pacific Rim, and one central Island base. Save the far north for another trip.

faqs.q: Do you need to book the ferry early?
a: Reserve vehicle space once dates are set, especially for weekends and holidays. Check the terminal and check-in window.

faqs.q: Which way should you go first on Vancouver Island?
a: Start in Victoria if you’re coming through Swartz Bay and finish near Nanaimo for the ferry back.

faqs.q: Can you stay on the west coast longer?
a: Yes. Trade the Campbell River section for two more coastal nights if beaches and boat tours are your main draw.

faqs.q: What should you do if you miss the lighthouse on Day 3?
a: Walk the loop early on Day 4 or save it for the morning you leave and shorten another stop.

title: Vancouver to Tofino and Ucluelet: 7-Day Road Trip
name: The Wild Coast Ferry Loop
meta: Drive from Vancouver to Tofino and Ucluelet in seven days, with time for Victoria and a return ferry from Nanaimo.
intro: If you’re starting in Vancouver, a week gives you time to see Victoria and still spend a few nights on the Island’s west coast. Using different ferry routes in each direction saves you the drive back to where you started. It’s a good loop for travelers with a car, especially if beaches and bluff walks are the main reason for going. Book both crossings, then keep the day you drive out to the coast free of set plans.

days.heading: Day 1: Vancouver

paras: Visit Long Beach and an open rainforest loop, then spend the rest of the day in Tofino. Drive back to Ucluelet for dinner.

title: Vancouver, Whistler, and the Sea-to-Sky Highway
